title: Level Gate Hysteresis Explorer
description: A level gate decides frame by frame whether the microphone hears speech. A single threshold opens at 15.0 bits and closes the moment the level dips back under it, so a voice that wobbles around the line makes the gate flutter. A hysteresis gate opens at the open level but closes only below a lower close level, so small dips inside a phrase do not close it.
creator: Dan McCreary

Level Gate
Hysteresis

learningObjectives: The learner will calculate how many times a single-threshold gate and a hysteresis gate change state on 3 loudness traces, matching the correct counts in 5 of 6 answers.
prerequisites: loudness in bits, frame, speech floor gate, level gate, hysteresis (all defined in this chapter above the block).

accessibility.notes: describe() provides a screen-reader description; all controls are native HTML elements.

controls.name: Trace menu, Open and Close sliders
controls.purpose: Explore only: traces A to C; open 13.0 to 18.0 bits and close 12.0 to 18.0 bits in steps of 0.1 (close is kept at or below open).

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Explore, then fixed-order practice items with one attempt each and immediate explained feedback
keyQuestions: Does hysteresis make the gate less sensitive to speech? What does it change?
Why did hysteresis not help in challenge 3?
Why does the gate open with >= and close with < ?
commonMisconceptions: (1) Hysteresis makes a gate less sensitive to speech. (2) Hysteresis removes every false opening. (3) The gate closes at the same level that it opens at.
assessmentOpportunities: Complete all three challenges. Mastery is 5 of the 6 counts correct on the first attempt.
